claim.summary: For continuous even real g of compact support with phi(s) = Re h(s + i/2) >= 0, h the transform of g: Re h(t+iy) = (1/2pi) int phi(s) K_y(t-s) ds with K_y(t) = 2 pi cos(pi y) cosh(pi t)/(sinh^2(pi t) + cos^2(pi y)); hence Re h(gamma + iy) >= cos(pi y) cos(pi delta) exp(-pi |gamma - gamma0|) Re h(gamma0 + i delta) in the open strip; and if the sum of Re h over a multiset Z of points of the strip is at most B while c Re h(gamma0 + i delta) > B, then cos(pi delta) sum over Z of cos(pi y_rho) exp(-pi |gamma_rho - gamma0|) < c.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (Fourier inversion, an explicit Poisson kernel of the strip, Harnack with constants), with a numerical control of the kernel and of the inequality. Limits explicit-formula certificates that require nonnegativity on the whole critical strip: they can exclude a point at distance delta from the line only where the weighted count of actual zeros near its height is below 4/cos(pi delta). The size of that count for zeta is recalled, not derived. Believed classical; no novelty claimed.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Answers the second route review's decisive test: positivity on the whole strip cannot separate a point from the zeros near it, so that formulation reproduces at best the classical region where the zeros nearby are on the line.
significance.next_action: Decide what a certificate needs when positivity is required only outside a window around the height.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry; one recalled integral checked numerically to 1.8e-10.

significance.note: Context: an obstruction to a method, elementary. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: The model's negative direction for the Gram form used positivity on the line only; this lemma shows the price of positivity on the strip.

claim.summary: Complete-grid Gram model, one off-axis pair of multiplicity m at distance delta and any real points, G = G_on + B: m(kappa+1) <= lambda_max(G) <= m(kappa+1) + lambda_max(G_on) and -m(kappa-1) <= lambda_min(G) <= min(0, -m(kappa-1) + eta), eta = e_y^T G_on e_y <= lambda_max(G_on); flat window: lambda_max(G_on) <= M_loc(3 + (2/pi)(1 + ln K)). So an operator-norm bound B at bandwidth Lam gives delta <= (log B + log(4 delta Lam))/Lam for a solitary pair with delta Lam >= 1, and a one-sided bound lambda_min >= -B the same with B + 1 + eta.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (test vectors e_x, e_y and Weyl). A small refinement of solitary amplification, whose part 4 already has the lower bound for lambda_max; added is the upper bound for lambda_min with its margin, and the observation that the extreme eigenvalues, unlike the second moment, see a solitary pair once kappa exceeds the on-line part's size, also at bandwidth log T. Complete grid only; the cut grid is not treated. The premise (an eigenvalue bound of size T^eps for the import's form) is not available, follows from the goal in the model, and is expected to be a local restatement of it.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Replaces the earlier reading that the Gram mechanism needs bandwidth beyond log T, which holds for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm only; names the premise at the import's own bandwidth.
significance.next_action: Derive the prime side of the quadratic form at bandwidth log T from the import's explicit formula and state which sum over prime powers bounds the extreme eigenvalues.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry for every window (the on-line bound for the flat window); control on 18 configurations, including real points denser than the grid.

significance.note: Context: a refinement that changes which premise the model's route needs; not a result about zeta. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: Refines solitary amplification (adds the upper bound for lambda_max and both bounds for lambda_min); uses the pair atom spectrum and the real configuration bound. The Gram form's prime side as a weighted square integral: new relationship with lem:prime-side-form-bound. Sign criteria for the logarithmic derivative of a finite configuration: new relationship with prop:log-derivative-sign-criteria. Harnack's inequality in the strip as a limit of positivity certificates: new relationship with lem:strip-positivity-obstruction.
